title: Photosynthesis
blurb: Photosynthesis turns light energy into chemical energy in autotrophs (overall equation; leaf and chloroplast structure; two phases).
lede: Photosynthesis turns light energy into chemical energy in autotrophs (overall equation; leaf and chloroplast structure; two phases). Light-dependent reactions in the thylakoids: the dual nature of light, PhAR 400–750 nm, pigments and their absorption, four ways an excited pigment loses energy, photosystems (LHC + reaction centre; PSI P700, PSII P680), the electron path through PSI (A0, A1, Fe–S, ferredoxin → NADP⁺) and PSII (pheophytin, plastoquinones, cytochrome b6/f, plastocyanin → P700), water photolysis (OEC), photophosphorylation, the Z-scheme (non-cyclic) and cyclic electron flow. Light-independent reactions in the stroma: the Calvin cycle (fixation by RuBisCO, reduction, regeneration), C3 plants and stomata, RuBisCO's oxygenase activity → photorespiration, and the adaptations C4 (spatial separation, Kranz anatomy) and CAM (temporal separation).

cards.lede: Read the question, answer it out loud, then flip the card.

items.n: Overall equation of photosynthesis?
items.a: 6 CO₂ + 12 H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂ + 6 H₂O.

items.n: Two phases of photosynthesis and their locations?
items.a: Light-dependent reactions (thylakoids) and light-independent reactions / Calvin cycle (stroma).

items.n: Products of the light reactions?
What is PhAR?
Three groups of photosynthetic pigments?
Four ways an excited pigment loses energy?
items.a: Kinetic energy, light/heat, energy transfer to another pigment, loss of the electron (charge separation).

items.n: Which pigment performs charge separation in the reaction centre?
Absorption maxima of PSI and PSII?
Electron path from PSI to NADP⁺?
items.a: P700* → A0 → A1 → Fe–S → ferredoxin → ferredoxin-NADP⁺ reductase → NADPH.

items.n: Where does PSI get its missing electron?
Electron path from PSII to PSI?
items.a: P680* → pheophytin → plastoquinone QA → QB → cytochrome b6/f → plastocyanin → P700.

items.n: Where does PSII get its missing electron?
Equation of water photolysis?
items.a: 2 H₂O → 4 H⁺ + 4 e⁻ + O₂ (at the oxygen-evolving complex).

items.n: What is photophosphorylation?
items.a: Light-driven ATP synthesis using the H⁺ gradient across the thylakoid membrane.

items.n: Where are protons accumulated in chloroplasts?
Cyclic vs non-cyclic electron flow?
items.a: Non-cyclic (Z-scheme): PSII + PSI, ATP + NADPH. Cyclic: PSI only, ATP only.

items.n: Where does the Calvin cycle occur, and what does it use?
items.a: In the stroma; it uses CO₂, ATP and NADPH.

items.n: Three phases of the Calvin cycle?
items.a: Carbon fixation, reduction, regeneration of RuBP.

items.n: Carbon fixation reaction?
What is reduced to G3P, and using what?
items.a: 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (made from 3-PGA with ATP) is reduced by NADPH to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate.

items.n: How many G3P regenerate how many RuBP?
What does RuBisCO stand for?
Share of leaf protein that is RuBisCO?
Carboxylation : oxygenation ratio of RuBisCO?
When does photorespiration dominate?
items.a: At low CO₂ and high O₂ (e.g. closed stomata in heat and drought).

items.n: Products of RuBP oxygenation?
Which organelles recycle 2-phosphoglycolate?
Benefits of photorespiration?
items.a: Protects against photo-oxidation damage and free radicals (though it costs ATP).

items.n: How do C4 plants separate CO₂ uptake and fixation?
items.a: Spatially: uptake in mesophyll, Calvin cycle in bundle-sheath cells (Kranz anatomy).

items.n: Examples of C4 plants?
First CO₂ acceptor in C4 and CAM plants?
How do CAM plants separate CO₂ uptake and fixation?
items.a: Temporally: CO₂ taken up at night (stomata open) and stored as malate; Calvin cycle by day (stomata closed).
